components.name: Dashboard Panel
components.description: The standard bordered container for one dashboard concern.
components.html:
Delivery health

Three sprints are active and one needs attention.
components.css: .ds-dashboard-panel { padding: 1.15rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--panel); color: var(--text); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 2%); font: 14px/1.55 var(--sans); } .ds-dashboard-panel h2 { margin: 0 0 .9rem; color: var(--text); font-size: 1.05rem; font-weight: 630; line-height: 1.3; letter-spacing: -.025em; } .ds-dashboard-panel p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); }

components.name: Linked Dashboard Panel
components.description: A whole-panel destination used only when no nested control conflicts.
components.html:
Project knowledge

3 dossiers

Requirements, technical design, and architecture.

Open project knowledge
components.css: .ds-dashboard-link { display: block; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; font: 14px/1.55 var(--sans); } .ds-dashboard-link section { padding: 1.15rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--panel); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 2%); transition: border-color .18s ease, background .18s ease, transform .18s cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1); } .ds-dashboard-link div { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; } .ds-dashboard-link h2 { margin: 0; color: var(--text); font-size: 1.05rem; } .ds-dashboard-link strong { color: var(--muted); font-size: .82rem; } .ds-dashboard-link p { color: var(--muted); } .ds-dashboard-link span { color: var(--accent-strong); font-size: .84rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-dashboard-link:hover section, .ds-dashboard-link:focus-visible section { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--panel-raised); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-dashboard-link:focus-visible { border-radius: var(--radius); outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Operational Button
components.description: A compact control placed beside the state it changes.
components.css: .ds-button { min-height: 2.25rem; padding: .45rem .75rem; border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: .5rem; background: var(--control); color: var(--text); box-shadow: inset 0 1px rgb(255 255 255 / 5%), 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 30%); font: 14px/1.55 var(--sans); cursor: pointer; } .ds-button:hover { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--control-hover); } .ds-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: A compact semantic state label with a matching dot.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: .35rem; padding: .13rem .48rem; border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: 999px; font: 620 .7rem/1.55 var(--sans); letter-spacing: .02em; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-status::before { content: ''; width: .38rem; height: .38rem; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; box-shadow: 0 0 7px currentColor; } .ds-status-active { color: var(--accent-strong); }

components.name: Segmented Progress
components.description: A truthful task distribution with separate workflow states.
components.css: .ds-segmented-progress { display: flex; width: 100%; min-height: .65rem; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--control); } .ds-segmented-progress i { min-width: 0; } .ds-complete { background: var(--success); } .ds-active { background: var(--accent-strong); } .ds-failed { background: var(--danger); } .ds-pending { background: var(--control); }

components.name: Evidence Preview
components.description: Content-height evidence rows with a label, summary, and path.
components.css: .ds-evidence { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; font: 14px/1.55 var(--sans); } .ds-evidence li a { display: grid; gap: .15rem; padding: .65rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-soft); color: var(--text); text-decoration: none; } .ds-evidence p { margin: .2rem 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: .76rem; } .ds-evidence span { overflow: hidden; color: var(--subtle); font-size: .7rem; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-evidence a:hover strong { color: var(--accent-strong); } .ds-evidence a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Attention Strip
components.description: A compact findings region reserved for work that needs inspection.
components.css: .ds-attention { padding: 1.15rem; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--warning) 35%, var(--border)); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--panel); color: var(--text); font: 14px/1.55 var(--sans); } .ds-attention div { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; } .ds-attention h2 { margin: 0; font-size: 1.05rem; } .ds-attention strong { color: var(--muted); font-size: .82rem; } .ds-attention p { margin: .75rem 0 0; color: var(--muted); }

components.name: Canonical QA Path
components.description: An eight-stage run map with direct anchors into retained QA facts and complete, active, pending, and failed states.
components.html:
1. AdmissionStage state: complete
  2. QA mapStage state: complete
  3. InvestigateStage state: active
  4. ChecksStage state: pending
  5. EvidenceStage state: pending
  6. SynthesisStage state: pending
  7. AdjudicationStage state: pending
  8. TerminalStage state: failed
components.css: .ds-qa-path { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; counter-reset: qa-stage; } .ds-qa-path li { position: relative; counter-increment: qa-stage; } .ds-qa-path a { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2.1rem minmax(0, 1fr); gap: .65rem; color: var(--muted); text-decoration: none; } .ds-qa-path i { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 2.1rem; height: 2.1rem; border: 2px solid var(--border); border-radius: 50%; background: var(--panel); font-style: normal; } .ds-qa-path i::before { content: counter(qa-stage); } .ds-qa-path [data-state=complete] i { border-color: var(--success); background: var(--success); color: var(--bg); } .ds-qa-path [data-state=complete] i::before { content: '✓'; } .ds-qa-path [data-state=active] i { border-color: var(--accent-strong); background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent-strong); box-shadow: 0 4px 18px color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 28%, transparent); animation: qa-stage-arrival 700ms cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) both; } .ds-qa-path [data-state=failed] i { border-color: var(--danger); color: var(--danger); } .ds-qa-path [data-state=failed] i::before { content: '!'; } @media (max-width: 64rem) { .ds-qa-path { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); } } @media (max-width: 48rem) { .ds-qa-path { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-qa-path * { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; } }

narrative.overview:
UltraPlan's project, sprint, and study overviews and its run detail pages are dark operating dashboards. They place current truth first, then expose the evidence needed to judge it. The interface is compact and calm. Fine borders and close tonal steps separate information without turning every fact into a card.

Each overview uses one dashboard grammar, but its previews keep the shape of the underlying work. A roadmap reads as a sequence, a sprint reads as staged execution, and a study reads as a research matrix. Actions sit inside the panel whose state they change. Linked panels become the navigation when they contain no competing controls.

Run pages use the same grammar at greater density. The QA command center begins with the canonical snapshot and ordered path, then keeps investigation records, synthesis, outcome, identity, and limits available through semantic disclosures. A historical run never borrows facts from the newer canonical pointer.
keyCharacteristics: One dominant current-state panel per entity overview
Truthful progress that distinguishes complete, active, failed, stale, and pending work
Canonical run paths that link stages directly to their retained facts
Content-shaped evidence previews instead of interchangeable statistic tiles
Compact attention regions reserved for findings and degraded health

rules.name: The State Color Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, pink, and strong magenta communicate workflow state. Do not use them to decorate neutral content.

rules.name: The Quiet Border Rule
rules.body: Separate ordinary regions with neutral borders. Warning-colored borders belong only on attention and degraded-health panels.

rules.name: The Numeric Truth Rule
rules.body: Counts and progress values use tabular numerals. Large type belongs to the state that matters now, not to decorative summary metrics.

rules.name: The Current State Rule
rules.body: Give one panel clear visual and spatial priority. It must answer what is happening now and what the next valid action is.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Borders and tonal layering establish ordinary hierarchy. Reserve a real shadow for the single dominant current-state panel.

rules.name: The Evidence Keeps Its Shape Rule
rules.body: Choose a preview that matches the underlying artifact or process. Do not replace timelines, matrices, sequences, or document excerpts with generic number cards.

rules.name: The Control Adjacency Rule
rules.body: An action belongs beside the state or object it changes. A panel with nested controls is not a whole-panel link.

rules.name: The Canonical Pointer Rule
rules.body: A run page shows canonical QA facts only when that run owns the current pointer. Never mix a historical event journal with a newer run's QA snapshot.

rules.name: The Live Disclosure Rule
rules.body: A live refresh may replace data, but it must not close a disclosure the operator opened or move focus out of the command center.

dos: **Do** make the dominant panel answer current state, progress, and next action with real workflow data.
**Do** preserve complete, active, failed, stale, and pending distinctions in progress previews.
**Do** keep all eight QA stages in canonical order and link each one to retained facts.
**Do** use content-shaped evidence such as timelines, matrices, stage rails, decision lists, and document excerpts.
**Do** make a control-free dashboard panel one coherent keyboard-focusable link.
**Do** keep actions inside the panel whose state they change.
**Do** preserve open QA disclosures during canonical live refresh.
**Do** stack panels in a truthful reading order below 48rem.
donts: **Don't** fill the overview with equal-weight metric cards.
**Don't** turn semantic state colors into decoration.
**Don't** hide failure, stale evidence, or waiting work inside a single completion percentage.
**Don't** let live runtime prose replace the canonical QA snapshot or retained evidence.
**Don't** show facts from the current canonical run inside a historical run page.
**Don't** wrap a panel in a link when it contains buttons, forms, or conflicting destinations.
**Don't** promote empty attention or healthy reliability into a dominant panel.
**Don't** use decorative shadows on ordinary dashboard panels.
